title: Kale, broccoli and cabbage are one plant
hook: Cabbage, kale, broccoli and Brussels sprouts are all the same species of plant.
peek: Wild cabbage grows on seaside cliffs in Europe. Over centuries, farmers bred it into cabbage, kale, broccoli, cauliflower, kohlrabi and Brussels sprouts, which are all still one species: Brassica oleracea.
lede: Cabbage, kale, broccoli, cauliflower, kohlrabi and Brussels sprouts look like different vegetables. Botanically they are one species, Brassica oleracea. They all descend from wild cabbage, a scrubby plant of the coasts of western and southern Europe. Over many centuries, farmers kept seed from the plants they liked best, and each line became a different vegetable.

bullets.text: Wild cabbage still grows on chalk and limestone sea cliffs in places such as southern England. It has thick, waxy leaves that help it hold water in salty, windy spots.

Each crop exaggerates one part of the same plant. Kale has big leaves, cabbage a huge tight end bud, Brussels sprouts many small side buds, kohlrabi a swollen stem, and broccoli and cauliflower thick clusters of flower buds.
Because they are one species, these vegetables can cross with one another. Seed growers keep them apart when they flower, or a field of cabbage can produce odd offspring.
Romanesco, a pale green relative of cauliflower, grows in spiralling cones made of smaller cones. The number of spirals usually matches a Fibonacci number, like the seed heads of sunflowers.
